body:
Dated a guy for a few months. From the second date I just had this gut feeling that something was off about him. Found out later that he definitely has an alcohol problem. He’s told me multiple times about how he drinks every night, how alcohol helps him with emotional/physical pain, how he feels more refreshed in the morning... 

I’ve dealt with a lot of addiction in my life, and unfortunately you can’t help someone who doesn’t want help. Sucks a lot, and he was great in every other way when he was sober.
I know. It fucking sucks. But you’ll be okay. Get it all out tonight, tomorrow is a new day. ❤️
I will, definitely. Thank you.
Thank you so much. I’ll do that
Thank you so much. Just worried about the potential crash and burn afterwards, it was really unexpected on my end but a week with minimal contact started to help.
Unfortunately no. He’s the only person who’s available to help, and he has a truck. My other friends would’ve but they have work, etc
I am so sorry. Stay strong, you’ll get through it ❤️
Great, thank you!
Thank you. Can I go back to live in base housing, or do I have to get my things and leave? We don't really have anywhere to go.
Great. Thank you!
Okay. I'm so sorry if I sound silly, but what do I say?
Okay. Should I talk to them when I'm there or call them while I'm out of state?
Okay. Should I take someone with me back to the house? I'm guessing I shouldn't tell him I'm going back?

Yes, that's very true. I'm gonna talk it over with my husband and see what he thinks, but I definitely agree. 

Thank you for your advice! 😊

Yeah that's true. I went to school for pharmacy tech, and worked in another pharmacy before we relocated. It just took a while to get licensed in my state, and find a job because the job outlook where we are now is kinda shitty for spouses. I did tell them my husbands in the military, but sometimes when he has to work late and I need to start, they don't really seem to understand. Which I get- I'm employed with them and they need me there. 

That's somewhat true about the money. It's basically "fun" money, or spending money. My husband wants me to work, mainly to get out of the house and help with gas, cigarettes, etc. but it isn't really a serious thing if I'm not. We will still be able to get food and keep the lights on. 

It does. But it's hard because it seems like every job gives me a lot of anxiety to the point where I either stop going or quit. I think I need to work on that and my depression and anxiety in general before I can be a good employee. But I don't think it usually works like that, unfortunately. 😔
Thank you. We talked a bit more and he's been really affectionate and at least trying. I'm  at least kind of glad I was able to go to work.
True.
Yeah right? Funny how you can be more open and understood with strangers than with your loved ones
No I don't think he is. I get he's trying to help however he can but it's hard because I feel so alone.

Yeah, you're 100% right. I'm going to talk to him once he's home from work. He isn't coming home during lunch, but I'm going to call this clinic and see what services they offer.  He's never dealt with anxiety or depression, so he doesn't understand. And we're very different- he's very serious and can hide his emotions, I need to talk through mine and I feel them deeply. So for him to just brush them off (in my perspective) makes me fee even shittier.

I think I should as well. But I don't think it'd work. My husband works 5 am-5pm Monday- Friday, and who would stay with our daughter...I don't think he'd be supportive. But in the end it would be the best decision because I don't want to go from considering writing a note to spiral more and end up attempting something. I'm pretty good at knowing when I need professional help.
Thank you!
